records.intervention_as_stated: purified soya lecithin, 20-25 g/day
records.population_as_stated: 51 subjects with senile dementia of the Alzheimer type
records.dose_quote: 20-25 g/day of purified soya lecithin (containing 90% phosphatidyl plus lysophosphatidyl choline) for six months
records.primary_result_quote: There were no differences between the placebo group and the lecithin group but there was an improvement in a subgroup of relatively poor compliers.
records.sample_size_quote: Fifty one subjects
records.direction_note: A post-hoc subgroup of older, poor compliers with intermediate plasma choline showed improvement; overall trial was negative.
records.label_material_note: Lecithin matches label material; high-dose purified soya lecithin monotherapy.

records.intervention_as_stated: soy lecithin, 25 g/day
records.dose_quote: 25 g (equivalent to 1.5 g omega-6, 0.5 g omega-3; omega-6/omega-3 ratio 3) per day of a soy lecithin supplement
records.primary_result_quote: In the soy lecithin group, platelet adhesion was increased in all test conditions (with ADP: from 18.7% to 23.2%, p<0.001; with thrombin: from 24.0% to 29.9% p<0.001; resting: from 3.5% to 6.6%, p<0.001).
records.sample_size_quote: we randomised 60 volunteers into three groups
records.direction_note: Soy lecithin significantly INCREASED platelet adhesion (a pro-thrombotic direction), opposite to the fish-oil comparator arm which decreased it -- notable safety-relevant finding.
records.label_material_note: Lecithin matches label material.

records.intervention_as_stated: lecithin
records.population_as_stated: 286 patients across 11 included RCTs (Alzheimer's and Parkinsonian dementia)
records.primary_result_quote: Evidence from randomised trials does not support the use of lecithin in the treatment of patients with dementia or cognitive impairment.
records.sample_size_quote: Eleven randomised trials have been identified involving patients with Alzheimer's disease (265 patients) and Parkinsonian dementia (21 patients).
records.label_material_note: Cochrane review restricted to unconfounded RCTs comparing lecithin with placebo.

records.direction_note: An updated Cochrane review version of 10796586; notes a dramatic positive result in one small trial of subjects with subjective memory problems.
records.label_material_note: Cochrane review restricted to unconfounded RCTs comparing lecithin with placebo.

records.label_material_note: Lecithin matches label material.

records.intervention_as_stated: soy lecithin, 600 or 1200 mg/day

records.indication_as_stated: soya-lecithin tolerance in non-IgE-mediated soya allergy
records.dose_quote: challenge dose of soya lecithin (1.5 g per day) in a custom-made biscuit
records.primary_result_quote: Over the challenge period, the parents reported reactions in six cases: five cases (23%) to the placebo and one case (5%) to the challenge dose.
records.sample_size_quote: Twenty-two children, 16 boys, with a median age of 44 months (range 21-58 months) were recruited
records.direction_note: Tolerance/allergy-challenge study rather than an efficacy trial; more reactions were reported to placebo than to the lecithin challenge, supporting tolerance.
records.label_material_note: Lecithin matches label material (soya lecithin food emulsifier).

handoff.reason: Soy lecithin 25 g/day significantly INCREASED platelet adhesion in all test conditions (resting and stimulated) versus a fish-oil comparator that decreased it -- a pro-thrombotic direction worth safety-review attention for high omega-6 lecithin intake.

identity_notes: Lecithin's retrieval set is dominated by a large false-match cluster around LCAT (lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase), an ENZYME etymologically named after lecithin but biologically and clinically unrelated to dietary lecithin supplementation -- this includes genetic LCAT deficiency case reports/reviews, and recombinant human LCAT enzyme DRUG trials (CSL112, MEDI6012, REAL-TIMI 63B), all rejected off_topic. A second large cluster is the fetal lung maturity lecithin/sphingomyelin (L/S) ratio, a diagnostic AMNIOTIC FLUID TEST for neonatal respiratory distress risk, not a supplementation intervention, also rejected off_topic. A third cluster is historical (1980s-90s) tacrine+lecithin and piracetam+lecithin combination trials for Alzheimer's disease, where lecithin is either a constant background co-treatment in both study arms or a minor adjunct to the primary drug being tested (tacrine/piracetam); these were rejected not_intervention since lecithin's own effect cannot be isolated -- the cleaner evidence for lecithin's own efficacy in dementia is the dedicated Cochrane reviews (10796586/11034695/12917896, three sequential updates of 'Lecithin for dementia and cognitive impairment'), all of which found NO clinical benefit, kept here as the authoritative synthesis. A recurring and important pattern for this identity is lecithin used as a PHOSPHOLIPID/PHYTOSOME DELIVERY VEHICLE for a different primary active (curcumin/Meriva, quercetin, boswellic acid/Casperome, bergamot polyphenols) -- in these records the clinical outcome is attributable to the co-administered active, not lecithin itself, so they are flagged related_form_differs and evidence_role reflects the primary active's indication; lecithin's bioavailability-enhancing role is noted in direction_note. A small but genuine single-ingredient oral lecithin evidence base exists for GI indications (phosphatidylcholine/enteric lecithin for ulcerative colitis: 33440385, 35831742 -- both positive) and for fatigue/menopausal symptoms (29310653, mixed results), plus one notable SAFETY signal: soy lecithin 25 g/day significantly increased platelet adhesion in a head-to-head comparison with fish oil (10595648, routed to handoff).
